title: One in three federated sign-ins to Teams fails at random
scenario: In a federated tenant about a third of attempts fail and the same user succeeds on the next click; one of three AD FS servers has a clock several minutes ahead, and resynchronising it ends the failures.

events.title: Call: one in three sign-ins failing
events.text: Call 14:05 UTC (16:05 local, CEST). Sofia Albrecht, IT lead at Marlow & Finch, reports that since about lunchtime (11:00 UTC) roughly one in three Teams sign-ins fails. It is random: the same person fails and then gets through on the very next click. About 35 people have complained so far. Their domain is federated with AD FS, three servers behind a load balancer. She has not looked at the AD FS servers yet.

events.title: Where I'd look first
events.text:
Hi Sofia, since sign-in goes through your own AD FS farm and only some attempts fail, please check each of the three nodes for certificate and time problems: expiry dates on the token-signing and service-communications certificates, w32tm /query /status on every node, and the AD FS admin event log since 11:00 UTC. I'd also like the exact error wording, three users who were hit with a UTC timestamp for each, and a note on whether any office fares worse than the others.

Mateo

events.title: AD FS node check
events.text:
Jonas (sysadmin at Marlow & Finch). Per node:

adfs01  w32tm offset +0.012s | certs valid until 2027-01-14 | admin log clean
adfs02  w32tm offset +487.3s, last successful sync 6 days ago | admin log: EventID 364 x212 since 11:04, 'security token time bounds invalid'
adfs03  w32tm offset +0.020s | certs valid until 2027-01-14 | admin log clean

adfs02 is the VM that was moved to another host last Thursday. Users who failed: j.keller@example.com 12:31 UTC, m.vogt@example.com 12:44, a.rossi@example.com 12:52. No difference between offices.

events.title: Sign-in log check
events.text: Sign-in logs for j.keller / m.vogt / a.rossi at 12:31 / 12:44 / 12:52 UTC: failure rows for all three, each citing the federated token's invalid time bounds. The successful retries right after were issued through other nodes. Fits adfs02 being about eight minutes ahead.

events.title: Cause and what to do
events.text:
Sofia - the cause looks clear: adfs02's clock is about eight minutes ahead, so tokens it issues are rejected downstream, and roughly a third of attempts land on it. Fix: resynchronise its time (and look at the hypervisor time-sync setting for that VM), and leave it out of rotation on the load balancer until its clock is right. I'll check back with you at 16:30 UTC.

Mateo

events.title: adfs02 resynced
events.text: adfs02 was pulled out of the pool at 15:52 UTC, resynced against the PDC, offset now +0.03s, and hypervisor time sync is switched off for that VM. Back in the pool at 16:20. Five of us have signed in to Teams ten times each since: no failures.

events.title: Next-day check
events.text:
Morning Sofia. The hourly count of federated failures in the sign-in logs has been flat at zero from 16:00 UTC yesterday onwards, and is still zero this morning. I also had Jonas re-run the clock check on all three nodes today: all within 50 ms. The case stays open until Friday as agreed.

Mateo

events.title: Re: Next-day check
events.text: Agreed, thanks. No complaints since yesterday afternoon.
